definitions.gloss: maybe so, could be, you might be right
definitions.explanation: A casual expression of tentative agreement or concession. The speaker acknowledges the possibility without fully committing to agreement. Short form of そうかもしれない.

examples.japanese: 「⟦{疲|つか}れ→疲れる：00901_tsukareru⟧てるん⟦じゃない→じゃない：28483_janai⟧？」「そうかも」
「⟦{電車|でんしゃ}→電車：00522_densha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ほう⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{早|はや}い→早い：00514_hayai⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧」「そうかも⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧」
「⟦もっと→もっと：00798_motto⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}した→練習する：22991_renshuusuru⟧⟦ほうがいい→ほうがいい：10078_hougaii⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}う→思う：00492_omou⟧」「そうかもしれない⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧」
examples.english: "I think you should practice more." "You might be right."

notes:
そうかも is a casual abbreviation of そうかもしれない (that may be the case). It expresses partial or tentative agreement — the speaker finds the idea plausible but is not fully convinced.

FORMS:
- そうかも: most casual, very common in conversation
- そうかも⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧: slightly softer, inviting shared agreement
- そうかもしれない: full form, slightly more considered
- そうかもしれません⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧: polite equivalent

AGREEMENT SPECTRUM:
Japanese has a gradient of agreement expressions:
- そうだ⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧ (full agreement) → そうかも (tentative) → そう⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧な (doubtful)

This spectrum allows speakers to modulate their stance smoothly without direct confrontation.
